question: Who among the following attended all the three Round Table Conferences held in London?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tej Bahadur Sapru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tej Bahadur Sapru was a prominent Indian lawyer, political leader, and freedom fighter known for his moderate views.
 
• He was one of the few Indian leaders who attended all three Round Table Conferences held in London between 1930 and 1932.
 
• Sapru played a significant role in the discussions, advocating for constitutional reforms and greater autonomy for India.
 
• His participation in all three conferences highlights his commitment to achieving a peaceful and negotiated settlement for India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Round Table Conferences:**

 
 
• The Round Table Conferences were a series of three conferences organized by the British Government to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• The first conference was held from November 1930 to January 1931, the second from September to December 1931, and the third from November to December 1932.
 
• These conferences were attended by representatives of the British government, Indian princely states, and various political parties in India.
 
• The main aim was to discuss the future governance of India and to reach a consensus on constitutional reforms.
 
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu:**
 
 
• She was an Indian independence activist, poet, and politician.
 
• Naidu was the first woman to become the president of the Indian National Congress and the first woman to serve as a governor in independent India.
 
• Although she was a prominent leader, she did not attend all three Round Table Conferences.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:**
 
 
• Gandhi was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and a proponent of non-violent civil disobedience.
 
• He attended only the second Round Table Conference held in 1931.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra Prasad:**
 
 
• Rajendra Prasad was an Indian independence activist, lawyer, and scholar who later became the first President of India.
 
• He did not attend any of the Round Table Conferences.
